_meta.author: Mistral Vibe (mistral-vibe)
_meta.purpose: Pilot taxonomy for the humanoid facet (LIBRARY.md Phases 1 and 4). v2 adds the depicted-vs-described clause to every entity facet: after the 2026-09-23 re-run, the fixed vision prompt correctly reports screenshots of text, but Jev still answered the scene the text describes (primary_subject=multiple at 0.91 on the known failure image). Only what the image itself shows counts.
design_notes: Entity type and representation are separate facets: a statue of a human is a depiction of a human, not a third kind of entity.
primary_subject includes 'multiple' because some images contain both a human and a robot (Buck and Twiki); a single-label taxonomy without it forces a wrong answer.
contains_human reuses the original criteria plus the depicted-vs-described clause, so the pilot remains a consistency check against the original run.

The depicted-vs-described clause is the only change from v1; representation definitions are untouched so the clause's effect is measurable in isolation (LIBRARY.md Phase 6 lesson: one revision, measured, not confounded).
All questions use the Choice schema; one call carries all five questions in a single parallel pass.

contains_human.instructions: Does this image contain a human?

criteria.yes: The image itself shows one or more humans (people, faces, bodies). Only what is visible in the image counts; a person who is merely mentioned, named, or described in text within the image does not count
criteria.no: The image itself shows no humans: no person, face, or body is visible in the image (people only mentioned or described in text do not count)

contains_robot.instructions: Does this image contain a robot or mechanical automaton?

criteria.yes: The image itself shows one or more robots: mechanical automatons, clearly manufactured machines with a body or face, whether photographed, illustrated, or rendered. Only what is visible counts; robots merely mentioned or described in text do not count
criteria.no: The image itself shows no robots or mechanical automatons (robots only mentioned in text do not count)

contains_android.instructions: Does this image contain an android: an artificial being that passes as human?

criteria.yes: The image itself shows one or more androids: artificial beings manufactured to pass as human, where the image or its context identifies them as artificial. Only what is visible counts; beings merely described in text do not count
criteria.no: The image itself shows no androids: no artificial beings presented as human-passing (beings only mentioned in text do not count)

primary_subject.instructions: What is the primary humanoid subject of the image?

criteria.human: The main subject the image itself shows is one or more humans; humans only mentioned or described in text do not count
criteria.robot: The main subject the image itself shows is one or more robots or mechanical automatons; robots only mentioned in text do not count
criteria.android: The main subject the image itself shows is one or more androids: artificial beings that pass as human
criteria.multiple: The image itself prominently shows more than one distinct kind of humanoid (e.g., a human together with a robot)
criteria.none: The image shows no humanoid subject of any kind: no human, robot, or android is visible in the image itself. Images that are only text, screenshots, objects, or scenes without humanoids are 'none' -- a humanoid described in text is not depicted

criteria.photograph: A photograph of a real scene: actual people, objects, or places captured by a camera
criteria.illustration: A drawing, cartoon, comic, painting, or digital illustration
criteria.statue_or_render: A statue, figurine, sculpture, model, or 3D render of a subject
criteria.text_screenshot: A screenshot or scan of text: the image shows words or code, not a scene
criteria.other: None of the above: a diagram, chart, map, abstract image, or interface screenshot without a depicted subject
